q: How much CBAM would an EU importer pay on Indian rebar using default values in 2026?
title: CBAM worked example: Indian rebar, 2026
short: About 3.37 certificates per tonne, or roughly EUR 277 at the third-quarter 2026 price of EUR 82.32. That is the India default of 4.270 plus the 10% mark-up, minus a free allocation adjustment of 0.975 x 1.364, assuming a correction factor of 1.0.
audience: EU importers of Indian TMT bar and the Indian mills that supply them

sections.h: The steps, per tonne of CN 7214 20 00
ol: Free allocation adjustment: 0.975 (CBAM factor) x 1.0 (correction factor) x 1.364 (benchmark, BF/BOF route) = 1.330

ul: The cross-sectoral correction factor is taken as 1.0, as listed in the Commission's Guidance No. 4. If the published 2026 value is lower, the deduction shrinks and the cost rises.
No carbon price paid in India is deducted, because India has none that qualifies.
The quarterly price depends on the quarter of import: EUR 75.36 for Q1, EUR 75.28 for Q2 and EUR 82.32 for Q3 2026.

p: Every tonne of verified emissions below the marked-up default removes about one certificate, because the free allocation deduction is set by benchmarks, not by the plant's own emissions. That gap is what an Indian supplier can offer in price negotiations.

senseible: Senseible reads coal, coke, gas, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so an actual figure you send an EU buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it. It does not file CBAM declarations.
